layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Curvilinear object segmentation is critical for many ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plications. However, manually annotating curvilinear ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects is very time-consuming and error-prone, yielding in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sufficiently available annotated datasets for existing super-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vised methods and domain adaptation methods. This pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: per proposes a self-supervised curvilinear object segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation method (FreeCOS) that learns robust and distinc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive features from fractals and unlabeled images. The key

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contributions include a novel Fractal-FDA synthesis (FFS)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: module and a geometric information alignment (GIA) ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proach. FFS generates curvilinear structures based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parametric Fractal L-system and integrates the generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures into unlabeled images to obtain synthetic train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing images via Fourier Domain Adaptation. GIA reduces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the intensity differences between the synthetic and unla-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beled images by comparing the intensity order of a given

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pixel to the values of its nearby neighbors. Such image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alignment can explicitly remove the dependency on abso-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lute intensity values and enhance the inherent geometric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics which are common in both synthetic and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: real images. In addition, GIA aligns features of synthetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and real images via the prediction space adaptation loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (PSAL) and the curvilinear mask contrastive loss (CMCL).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extensive experimental results on four public datasets, i.e.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XCAD, DRIVE, STARE and CrackTree demonstrate that our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method outperforms the state-of-the-art unsupervised meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods, self-supervised methods and traditional methods by a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: large margin. The source code of this work is available at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: https://github.com/TY-Shi/FreeCOS.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Automatically segmenting curvilinear structures (such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as vascular trees in medical images and road systems in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aerial photography) is critical for many applications, in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cluding retinal fundus disease screening [2, 14], diagnosing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coronary artery disease [38], road condition evaluation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintenance [51]. Despite a plethora of research works in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the literature, accurately segmenting curvilinear objects re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mains challenging due to their complex structures with nu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: merous tiny branches, tortuosity shapes, ambiguous bound-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aries due to imaging issues and noisy backgrounds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leverage supervised deep learning for curvilinear object seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation and have achieved encouraging results. However,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those methods require a large number of pixel-wise manual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations for training which are very expensive to obtain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and error-prone due to poor image quality, annotator's fa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tigue and lack of experience. Although, there are several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: publically available annotated datasets for curvilinear object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation [37, 17, 51, 25], the large appearance vari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ations between different curvilinear object images, e.g., X-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ray coronary angiography images vs. retinal fundus images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yields significant performance degradation for supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models across different types of images (even across the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same type of images acquired using different equipments).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As a result, expensive manual annotations are inevitably de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manded to tune the segmentation model for a particular ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plication. Potential solutions to alleviate the annotation bur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: den include domain adaption [8, 32] and unsupervised seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation [9, 19, 24, 11, 9, 1]. However, the effectiveness

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of domain adaptation is largely dependent on the quality of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotated data in the source domain and constrained by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gap between the source and target domain. Existing unsu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pervised segmentation methods [9, 19] can hardly achieve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfactory performance for curvilinear objects due to their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thin, long, and tortuosity shapes, complex branching struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, and confusing background artifacts.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite the high complexity and great variety of curvi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linear structures in different applications, they share some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: common characteristics (i.e., the tube-like shape and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branching structure). Thus, existing studies [47, 46, 48]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have demonstrated that several curvilinear structures (e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: arterial trees of the circulation system) can be generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: via the fractal systems with proper branching parameters

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to mimic the fractal and physiological characteristics, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: †Corresponding author.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some observed variability. These results motivate us to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use the generated curvilinear objects via the fractal sys-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tems to explicitly encode geometric properties and varieties

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (i.e., different diameters and lengths of branches, and dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferent branching angles) into training samples and to as-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sist feature learning of a curvilinear structure segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model. However, such formulas generated training samples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can hardly mimic the appearance patterns within curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects, the transition regions between curvilinear objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and backgrounds, which are also key information for learn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing a segmentation model and contained in easily-obtained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unlabeled target images. This paper asks the question, how

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to combine fractals and unlabeled target images to encode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sufficient and comprehensive visual cues for learning robust

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and distinctive features of curvilinear structures?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The main contribution of this paper is a self-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation method based on a novel Fractal-FDA syn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thesis (FFS) module and a geometric information alignment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (GIA) approach. Specifically, curvilinear structures are syn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thesized by the parametric fractal L-Systems [47]and serve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as segmentation labels of synthetic training samples. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simulate appearance patterns in the object-background tran-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sition regions and background regions, we apply Fourier

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Domain Adaptation [45] (FDA) to fuse synthetic curvilinear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures and unlabeled target images. The synthetic im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages via our FFS module can effectively guide learning dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinctive features to distinguish curvilinear objects and back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grounds. To further improve the robustness to differences

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between intensity distributions of synthetic and real target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images, we design a novel geometric information alignment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (GIA) approach which aligns information of synthetic and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: target images at both image and feature levels. Specifically,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GIA first converts each training image (synthetic and target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images) into four geometry-enhanced images by compar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the intensity order of a given pixel to the values of its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nearby neighbors (i.e., along with the up, down, left and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: right directions). In this way, the four converted images do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not depend on the absolute intensity values but the relative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity in order to capture the inherent geometric charac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teristic of the curvilinear structure, reducing the intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences between synthetic and target images. Then, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extract features from the 4-channel converted images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: propose two loss functions, i.e., a prediction space adap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation loss (PSAL) and a curvilinear mask contrastive loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (CMCL), to align the geometric features of synthetic and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: target images. The PSAL minimizes the distance between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the segmentation masks of the target images and synthetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curvilinear objects and the CMCL minimizes the distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between features of segmented masks and synthetic objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The FreeCOS based on FFS and GIA approaches ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plies to several public curvilinear object datasets, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: XCAD [25], DRIVE [37], STARE [17] and CrackTree [51].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extensive experimental results demonstrate that FreeCOS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outperforms the state-of-the-art self-supervised [25, 21],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: unsupervised [9, 19], and traditional methods [13, 22]. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: summarize, the main contributions of this work are as fol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose a novel self-supervised curvilinear feature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning method which intelligently combines tree-like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fractals and unlabeled images to assist in learning ro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bust and distinctive feature representations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We propose Fractal-FDA synthesis (FFS) and geomet-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ric information alignment (GIA), which are the two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: key enabling modules of our method. FFS integrates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the synthetic curvilinear structures into unlabeled im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages to guide learning distinctive features to distin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guish foregrounds and backgrounds. GIA enhances

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: geometric features and meanwhile improves the fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture robustness to intensity differences between syn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thetic and target unlabeled images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We develop a novel self-supervised segmentation net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work that can be trained using only target images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and fractal synthetic curvilinear objects. Our network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performs significantly better than state-of-the-art self-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised/unsupervised methods on multiple public

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets with various curvilinear objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. Traditional Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Traditional curvilinear object segmentation methods [20,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 26, 13, 40, 22] design heuristic rules and/or filters to cap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture features of the target curvilinear objects. For instance,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Frangi et al. introduce the vesselness filter [13] based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Hessian matrix to represent and enhance tube-like curvilin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ear objects. Khan et al. [20] further design B-COSFIRE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: filters to denoise retinal images and segment retinal ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sels. Memari et al. [26] enhance image contrast via contrast-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited adaptive histogram equalization and then segment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal vessels based on hand-crafted filters. In [40, 22], the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: authors propose optimally oriented flux (OOF) to enhance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curvilinear tube-like objects. OOF exhibits better perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance for segmenting adjacent curvilinear objects yet is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensitive to different sizes of curvilinear objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Traditional methods based on hand-crafted filters do not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require any training yet they require careful parameter tun-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing for optimized performance. And the optimized pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rameter settings are usually data-dependent or even region-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dependent, limiting their convenience in segmenting a wide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variety of curvilinear objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2. Unsupervised Segmentation Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unsupervised segmentation methods can be generally di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vided into two classes: clustering based [19, 24, 11] and ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1. The pipeline of Self-Supervised Learning from Fractals and Unlabeled Images for Curvilinear Object Segmentation (FreeCOS).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: versarial learning based [9, 1]. Xu et al. [19] propose Invari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ant Information Clustering (IIC) which automatically parti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions input images into regions of different semantic classes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by optimizing mutual information between related region

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pairs. Such a clustering-based method is more suitable for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmenting objects with aspect ratios close to one while be-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coming ineffective for curvilinear objects due to their thin,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: long, tortuous shapes. Redo [9] is based on an adversarial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: architecture where the generator is guided by an image and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extracts the object mask, then redraws a new object at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same location with different textures/colors. However, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adversarial learning-based unsupervised method only per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forms well for objects which are visually distinguishable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from backgrounds. For the segmentation of curvilinear ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects with complex and numerous tiny branching structures,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embedded in confusing and cluttered backgrounds, the effi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cacy of such a method degrades significantly.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In contrast to unsupervised methods, our method explic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itly encodes geometric and photometric characteristics, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as some observed varieties of curvilinear objects in tar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: get application into synthetic images. Those synthetic im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages provide labels to effectively guide the model to learn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robust and distinctive features and thus yield superior per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formance to state-of-the-art unsupervised methods [9, 19].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.3. Self-supervised Learning Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Self-supervised learning methods construct pretexts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from large-scale unsupervised data and utilize contrastive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning losses to measure the similarities of sample pairs in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the representation space. To this end, various pretext tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been designed, including jigsaw [12], hole-fill [31]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and transformation invariance [16]. Although existing self-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervised methods have achieved outstanding performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in classification [27, 4], detection [44, 5], and image trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lation [30, 43], few of them provide a suitable pretext

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: task for curvilinear object segmentation. A potential solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion is the pixel-level contrastive-based method [41, 3, 49],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while it requires heavy manual annotations to prepare pixel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: level positive and negative samples. Similar work to ours

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is [25, 21] which designs a self-supervised vessel segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation method via adversarial learning and fractals. But this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method requires clean background images as input (i.e.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the first frame of the angiography sequence) for synthesis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which greatly limits its applications. In addition, adversarial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning cannot explicitly and precisely enforce visual cues,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are important for learning segmentation-oriented fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, being encoded in the synthetic images. As a result,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: although their synthetic images visually look similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: target images, the segmentation accuracy is also quite low.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure. 1 shows the framework of FreeCOS which con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sists of two main modules, i.e., Fractal-FDA Synthesis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (FFS) and Geometric Information Alignment (GIA). In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FFS, we generate synthetic curvilinear structures via the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parametric Fractal L-Systems and use the generated struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures as segmentation maps to guide self-supervised training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a segmentation network. The synthetic curvilinear struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures are then integrated into unlabeled images via FDA to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form synthetic images of curvilinear structures. The in-

layout_dets.text: We further explore the importance of different param-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eters in FFS on the final performance and discuss how to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate images of curvilinear structures to encode suffi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cient and comprehensive visual cues for learning robust and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distinctive features. To this end, we build 6 variant models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on FFS. 1) FFS w/o Gaussian blur. We do not per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form Gaussian blur to synthetic images from FFS. 2) FFS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: w/o FDA. We remove FDA-based synthesis from FFS and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only generate curvilinear structures without backgrounds.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) FFS w/o various intensities. We remove intensity varia-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the Fractal system and set the intensity to a fixed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: value 60. 4) FFS w/o various angles. We utilize a small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: branching angle range from (1°, 5°) to reduce the branching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: angle variations. 5) FFS w/o various lengths. We reduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the length variation range to (10px, 20px). 6) FFS w/o var-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ious widths. We reduce the width variation to (1px, 5px).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results in Table 5 show that 1) Gaussian blur can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: smooth the transition region between curvilinear objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and backgrounds, better mimicking the target images and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: providing more challenging samples for training than those

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with sharp boundaries. As a result, excluding Gaussian blur

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreases the performance of FFS by 6.8% in Dice. 2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FDA could provide background patterns of target images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which are essential for learning features of negative sam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ples. Thus, FFS w/o FDA is 15.6% worse than FFS in Dice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3) Among the four parameters of the Fractal system, i.e.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity, angle, length and width, width plays the most im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: portant role in the final performance, i.e., FFS w/o various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: widths decreases the performance by 26.1% compared with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FFS in Dice. To summarize, we identify that the appear-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ance patterns in the curvilinear object, object-background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transition regions and background regions are important for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self-supervised segmentation. Meanwhile, proper parame-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ter settings which can provide similar geometric character-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: istics with the real target images are key to the success of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our self-supervised method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3.3 Ablation Study on Architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: By replacing the U-Net with Iternet in FFS, We conduct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ablation studies on two backbone networks U-Net [33]

layout_dets.label: inline_formula
layout_dets.latex: \mathrm { F F S + G I A }

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Iternet [23]. FFS using Iternet segmentation model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gets better performance than FFS using U-Net in Table 6.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also demonstrates performance improvement,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: showing FreeCOS's effectiveness on different architectures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This indicates that the use of a more advanced segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion network architecture for FreeCOS has the potential to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3.4 Self-supervised training with more data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We also examine the segmentation performance when vary-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the number of synthetic images on the XCAD dataset.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Results in Tables. 7 and 8 provide the results when us-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing different numbers of synthetic structures and real target

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images for generating synthetic images for self-supervised

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training respectively. Synthetic-15~ Synthetic-150 denote

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using the number of synthetic fractal object images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from 15 to 150, and Target-162 ~ Target-1620 denote us-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing the number of target images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from 162 to 1620. In-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creasing both synthetic structures and real target images can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accordingly improve the final segmentation performance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose a novel self-supervised curvi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linear object segmentation method (FreeCOS) that learns

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: robust and distinctive features from fractals and unlabeled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. Different from existing methods, FreeCOS applies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the proposed FFS and GIA approach to effectively guide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning distinctive features to distinguish curvilinear ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects and backgrounds and aligns information of synthetic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and target images at both image and feature levels. One

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limitation of FreeCOS is that may generate false positives in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other curvilinear objects (e.g., catheters in XCAD) and re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quires proper selection for width range. However, we have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: successfully utilized this self-supervised learning method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for coronary vessel segmentation, retinal vessel segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and crack segmentation by reasonable parameter selec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. To the best of our knowledge, FreeOCS is the first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self-supervised learning method for various curvilinear ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject segmentation applications.
